# Implementation Plan: Fix crews lead reply-to asymmetry (consumed-inbox-envelope ids)

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-07. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan <job_dir>/plan.md`.*

## Overview

A crews **lead** that replies to a CONSUMED proactive member report (`kind=question|blocked|done`)
throws `ReplyToNotFoundError` when it uses the same mailbox-envelope id that `review-mail` surfaces
as the "actionable ack/reply id". This breaks two lead surfaces:

1. `node crews.js send-to-member <member> --reply-to <envelope-id>` (direct send), and
2. `<|report reply-to="<envelope-id>"|>` on the lead's Stop turn.

Root cause: `resolveReplySource(sender, replyTo, cwd)` in `hooks/mailbox.js` — the
`sender.role === 'lead'` branch searches only the lead's send-history
(`getSendHistoryPath`) + member outboxes (`memberOutboxRowsIncludingLeftAt`), but **never** the
lead's own consumed mailbox-history (`getInboxHistoryPath`). The `sender.role === 'member'` branch
DOES search `getInboxHistoryPath`. Meanwhile `ack=<id>` resolves the same id, because STRICT-ACK
matches ack ids against consumed-this-turn mailbox-history entries — a path that does NOT go
through `resolveReplySource`. So `ack` and `reply-to` are inconsistent on the exact id `review-mail`
tells the lead to use.

This plan implements **Option A**: extend the lead branch of `resolveReplySource` to ALSO resolve
against the lead's consumed mailbox-history, making any surfaced envelope id uniformly usable for
BOTH `ack` and `reply-to` — without breaking STRICT-ACK or the existing AskUserQuestion
(`member-question-request`) carve-out. Plugin-side only (`ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews`).

## Research Findings

### Codebase Context (all paths under `ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/crews/`)

**`resolveReplySource` — the defect (`hooks/mailbox.js:358-376`):**
```js
function resolveReplySource(sender, replyTo, cwd) {
  if (!replyTo) return null;
  if (sender.role === 'member') {
    const rows = readJsonLinesStrict(getInboxHistoryPath(sender.name, sender.crew, cwd));
    const found = findMessageById(rows, replyTo);
    if (!found) throw new ReplyToNotFoundError(replyTo);
    return found;
  }
  if (sender.role === 'lead') {
    const ownRows = readJsonLinesStrict(getSendHistoryPath(sender.name, sender.crew, cwd));
    const own = findMessageById(ownRows, replyTo);
    if (own) return own;
    const memberRows = memberOutboxRowsIncludingLeftAt(sender.crew, cwd);
    const member = findMessageById(memberRows, replyTo);
    if (member) return member;
    throw new ReplyToNotFoundError(replyTo);   // <-- thrown for a consumed inbox id
  }
  throw new ReplyToNotFoundError(replyTo);
}
```

**Two call sites both funnel through `resolveReplySource` (the entire bug surface is this one
function):**
- `appendMailboxWithSender` (`hooks/mailbox.js:446-447`) — the `/send-to-member --reply-to`
  DIRECT send path. `noReplyResolution` is true only for `sender.role === 'system' | 'operator'`;
  a lead is neither, so it calls `resolveReplySource` and throws. **This path has NO stop.js
  suppression layer**, so it can only be fixed by changing `resolveReplySource`.
- `buildOutboxEntry` (`hooks/mailbox.js:715-716`) via `appendOutboxBatch` (`:736-781`) — the Stop
  `<|report reply-to|>` path. The throw propagates up to `hooks/stop.js:1356-1362`, which catches it
  and emits `{decision:'block', reason: e.message}` — i.e. it BLOCKS the lead's whole turn.

**`deriveHops` + inbox-history row shape — confirms an inbox-resolved source is safe:**
- `deriveHops(replyTo, source)` (`hooks/mailbox.js:378-383`):
  `const hops = (Number.isFinite(source && source.hops) ? source.hops : 0) + 1;`
- `consumeMailbox` writes inbox-history rows at `hooks/mailbox.js:682`:
  `appendJsonLineStrict(historyPath, Object.assign({}, envelope, { seq, receivedAt, consumedAt, via }))`.
  Because the row spreads the original `envelope`, it carries the envelope's `id` (matches the
  surfaced "actionable id") AND its `hops` field. So a lead resolving against inbox-history yields a
  row whose `id` matches `findMessageById` and whose `hops` feeds `deriveHops` correctly.

**Turn-resolution is ALREADY independent of `resolveReplySource`, AND proactive-reports are
STRICT-ACK auto-exempt:**
- `evaluateConsumedResolutions(pendingConsumed, reports, decisionRows)` (`hooks/stop.js:288-312`,
  invoked at `:1058`) resolves a consumed entry by matching the **in-tag** `reply-to`/`ack`/decision
  against the entry id (`findCurrentDecision` `:267-269`). It never calls `resolveReplySource`.
- **`ACK_EXEMPT_KINDS` (`hooks/stop.js:189-196`) includes `proactive-report`** (plus `member-reply`,
  `thread-fanout`, `thread-notification`, `member-left`, `member-joined`); `isAckExempt(entry)`
  (`:263-264`) requires `entry.from.role === 'system'` AND that routingKind set. A consumed
  proactive-report (`from.role:'system'`, `routingKind:'proactive-report'`) is therefore AUTO-EXEMPT:
  `evaluateConsumedResolutions` SKIPS it at `:294` (`if (isAckExempt(entry)) continue;`) and writes
  NO `decision:"replied"` mailbox-decision row for it.
- Consequence: a lead does NOT need to reply-to/ack a consumed proactive-report for STRICT-ACK (the
  turn is not blocked by the unresolved-consumed gate regardless). The bug is that IF the lead chooses
  to thread `reply-to=<envelope-id>` (the id `review-mail` surfaces), the **durable outbox write**
  (`appendOutboxBatch`→`buildOutboxEntry`→`resolveReplySource`) THROWS `ReplyToNotFoundError` and
  blocks the whole turn. The fix is purely "stop the write from throwing"; it does NOT (and must not)
  start writing a decision row for the exempt entry.
- A NON-exempt consumed message (e.g. a `kind="direct"` message delivered to the lead) is the only
  Stop-path case where reply-to BOTH resolves the consumed entry into a `decision:"replied"` row AND
  must resolve through `resolveReplySource` — so the regression suite needs that case to cover the
  decision-row path.

**The `member-question-request` carve-out (`hooks/stop.js:314-323`, `:1316-1318`):**
```js
function isSystemAckOnlyReplyTo(replyTo, entries) {
  if (!replyTo) return false;
  return (entries || []).some(entry =>
    entry && entry.id === replyTo &&
    entry.from && entry.from.role === 'system' &&
    entry.from.routingKind === 'member-question-request');
}
// ...
let effectiveReplyTo = report.replyTo;
if (state.role === 'lead' && isSystemAckOnlyReplyTo(effectiveReplyTo, pendingConsumed)) effectiveReplyTo = null;
```
This nulls the lead's OUTBOX-ROW `replyTo` for AskUserQuestion-routed questions (which are
`from.role: 'system'`), because the lead delivers the actual answer via a separate
`/send-to-member` and the report-tag `reply-to` is a pure resolution marker. The turn still
resolves (via the raw in-tag `report.replyTo`, not `effectiveReplyTo`). It is ALSO why those ids
don't hit the throw today — `effectiveReplyTo=null` reaches `buildOutboxEntry`, so
`resolveReplySource` never sees them. A regular proactive-report is `from.role: 'member'`,
`routingKind: 'proactive-report'`, so `isSystemAckOnlyReplyTo` returns false → no suppression →
the throw fires. (See AGENTS.md v1.3.8.)

**Downstream member-reply routing is member-only (decides the A2 sub-question):**
- The per-row reply-notification block at `hooks/stop.js:1431-1457` is gated `state.role ===
  'member'`. For each member-written row with `row.replyTo`, it calls
  `findActorBySendHistoryId(crew, cwd, row.replyTo)` and notifies the addressed lead.
- The proactive-report routing block (`:1459-1505`) is also `state.role === 'member'`.
- **There is NO lead per-row routing that reads a lead's outbox-row `replyTo`.** So persisting
  `replyTo=<inbox-envelope-id>` on a lead row is inert downstream — no
  `findActorBySendHistoryId(<inbox-id>)` lookup runs on it that could fail.

**`review-mail` surfacing (`hooks/commands/review-mail.js:103-122`, expansion `:153-165`):** the
"actionable id" exposed to the lead is the mailbox-envelope `id`; `outboxId`/`reportId`/`outboxSeq`
are the member outbox references, `inboxSeq` is the consumed mailbox-history seq. This is the UI
contract that makes Option A the right fix (Option B would fight this output shape and force the lead
to learn two ids).

### Technical Constraints
- `ReplyToNotFoundError` (`hooks/errors.js:135-140`) must stay fail-loud for genuinely unknown ids
  (typos, ids not visible to the sender). The fix only ADDS the inbox-history source; it must still
  throw when the id is in none of send-history / member-outboxes / inbox-history.
- UUID ids cannot collide across the three sources, so search order only affects which source's
  `hops` is used; for a consumed proactive-report only inbox-history has it.
- The `member` branch is unchanged. Only the `lead` branch gains the third lookup.
- This is the `ai-developer-toolkit` SUBMODULE. Implementation requires the two-commit flow:
  commit + push inside the submodule first, then a codexu pointer bump (lead-owned per AGENTS.md).
- crews has no `package.json`; "typecheck" = `node --check <changed-js-file>` per crews AGENTS.md.

## Approach

### Architecture
Add a third lookup to the **lead** branch of `resolveReplySource` only: after the send-history and
member-outbox misses, read the lead's own consumed mailbox-history (`getInboxHistoryPath(sender.name,
sender.crew, cwd)`) and `findMessageById`. Return the found row (carrying `id` + `hops`); otherwise
keep the existing `throw new ReplyToNotFoundError(replyTo)`. This mirrors the `member` branch and the
ack resolution path, making the surfaced "actionable id" uniformly usable for both `ack` and
`reply-to`.

**A2 decision — keep the `member-question-request` carve-out, do NOT add a new suppression:**
- KEEP `isSystemAckOnlyReplyTo` + the `effectiveReplyTo=null` line (`stop.js:1317`) untouched. With
  the resolver extended, member-question-request ids would now also resolve, but the carve-out nulls
  `effectiveReplyTo` *before* `buildOutboxEntry`, so behavior for that envelope kind is byte-identical
  to today (no persisted back-reference, no Roundtrip-B regression).
- Do NOT generalize the suppression to other inbox-resolved ids. PRESERVE the outbox-row `replyTo`
  for general inbox-resolved ids because (a) the direct `/send-to-member --reply-to` path needs the
  `replyTo` to thread/wake the member — nulling it there would lose the linkage; and (b) on the Stop
  path the lead per-row routing is member-only (`stop.js:1431`), so persisting `replyTo` is inert and
  yields a correct hop chain (useful audit metadata). This keeps the change to a single function.

### Implementation Strategy
1. Extend the lead branch of `resolveReplySource` (one added lookup + a forensic comment).
2. Add a focused unit regression test for the resolver (lead reply-to resolves a consumed
   inbox-history id; still throws for a truly-unknown id; member branch unchanged).
3. Add Stop-path integration regression tests covering BOTH STRICT-ACK classes:
   (a) EXEMPT — lead consumes a proactive `kind=question`, replies via
   `<|report reply-to="<envelope-id>"|>`; assert: no `ReplyToNotFoundError`/no block, the outbox row
   persists the resolved `replyTo` + sane `hops`, and NO `decision:"replied"` row is written (the
   entry is ack-exempt); and (b) NON-EXEMPT — lead consumes a `kind="direct"` message, replies via
   `reply-to=<that-id>`; assert: no throw, a `decision:"replied"` row IS written, outbox row persists
   `replyTo`/`hops`. Plus a direct-send test (`appendMailbox` with `sender.role==='lead'` +
   `replyTo: <consumed-inbox-id>` succeeds — the `/send-to-member --reply-to` path, which is unaffected
   by STRICT-ACK exemption and is the cleanest standalone demonstration of the resolver fix).
4. Keep the `member-question-request` carve-out test(s) green (regression guard that it still nulls
   the outbox-row `replyTo`).
5. Standard crews version bump (6 stamps + `tests/version.test.js`) via
   `node plugins/crews/scripts/bump-version.js <x.y.z>` + CHANGELOG entry + AGENTS.md section.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Extending the lead branch of `resolveReplySource` to resolve consumed mailbox-history ids.
- Regression tests for both failing call sites + a carve-out regression guard.
- 6-file version bump + `version.test.js` + CHANGELOG + AGENTS.md note (plugin-side only).

### Out of Scope
- Option B (re-surfacing the member outbox id as the canonical reply target in `review-mail`).
- Any change to the `member` branch of `resolveReplySource`, to `deriveHops`, or to STRICT-ACK
  resolution semantics.
- Generalizing or removing the `member-question-request` carve-out.
- Adding lead per-row member-reply routing (routing the lead's reply back to the member is a
  separate, out-of-scope enhancement).
- Any codexu-root or non-crews edits beyond the lead-owned submodule pointer bump. The impl member
  must NOT `git add` the gitignored codexu `CLAUDE.md`; fork-guidance edits go in codexu `AGENTS.md`
  (lead-owned, not the impl member).

## Risk Areas
- **STRICT-ACK exemption (most important — caught in Phase-4 review).** Proactive-reports are
  ack-exempt (`stop.js:189-196` + `:263-264` + skip at `:294`). The fix must NOT cause a decision row
  to be written for a consumed proactive-report, and tests must NOT assert one. The decision-row path
  is exercised only via a NON-exempt consumed message (AC2b). Mis-specifying this (the original draft
  did) yields a test that can never pass.
- **Regressing fail-loud behavior.** Must still throw `ReplyToNotFoundError` for ids in NONE of the
  three sources. Covered by an explicit negative test (AC4).
- **Member-question-request regression.** The carve-out must stay green. Covered by a guard test
  asserting the outbox row still nulls `replyTo` for that envelope kind (AC5).
- **Hop-chain correctness.** Inbox-history rows carry `hops`; verify the resolved row produces
  `source.hops + 1`. Covered by asserting `hops` on the written row (AC2).
- **Search-order subtlety.** Inbox lookup must be LAST (after send-history + member-outboxes) so the
  lead's own prior sends / known member outbox rows keep priority. (UUIDs can't collide, so this is
  defensive ordering, not strict correctness.)
- **Windows test flake.** crews suite is race-sensitive; capture output to a log on first run and
  grep, per repo AGENTS.md.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: A lead calling `resolveReplySource` with the id of a consumed inbox-history proactive-report
  returns that row (no throw); `node --check hooks/mailbox.js` passes.
- AC2: A lead's Stop turn `<|report kind="done" reply-to="<consumed-envelope-id>"|>` for a consumed
  `kind=question` PROACTIVE-REPORT does NOT throw `ReplyToNotFoundError` / does NOT produce
  `{decision:'block'}`; the outbox row is written with `replyTo === <envelope-id>` and
  `hops === sourceHops + 1`. NOTE: proactive-reports are STRICT-ACK auto-exempt
  (`stop.js` `ACK_EXEMPT_KINDS` includes `proactive-report`; `isAckExempt` requires
  `from.role==='system'`), so `evaluateConsumedResolutions` SKIPS the entry — the test MUST assert
  that NO `decision:"replied"` mailbox-decision row is written for that proactive-report envelope id
  (asserting one would be wrong). The "resolution" here is the resolver returning the inbox row +
  the outbox row persisting `replyTo`/`hops`, not a decision row.
- AC2b: For a NON-exempt consumed message (e.g. a `kind="direct"` message delivered to the lead's
  mailbox), a lead Stop turn `<|report ... reply-to="<that-id>"|>` does NOT throw, AND a
  `decision:"replied"` mailbox-decision row IS written for that id (STRICT-ACK resolution recorded),
  AND the outbox row persists `replyTo`/derived `hops`. This is the path that exercises both the
  resolver fix AND decision-row recording (proactive-reports cannot, because they are exempt).
- AC3: A lead direct send `appendMailbox(..., { replyTo: <consumed-inbox-id> })` (the
  `/send-to-member --reply-to` path) succeeds and stamps the delivered envelope `replyTo` +
  derived `hops` (no `ReplyToNotFoundError`).
- AC4: `resolveReplySource` still throws `ReplyToNotFoundError` for an id present in none of
  send-history / member-outboxes / inbox-history.
- AC5: The `member-question-request` carve-out is unchanged — a lead reply-to that references a
  `member-question-request` system envelope still writes a NULL outbox-row `replyTo` (existing
  behavior preserved; guard test green).
- AC6: The `member` branch of `resolveReplySource` is behaviorally unchanged (existing
  `tests/reply-to.test.js` and member-reply tests stay green).
- AC7: Version bumped across all 6 stamps + `tests/version.test.js` green; CHANGELOG entry prepended;
  AGENTS.md note added.
- AC8: Full crews suite (`node plugins/crews/tests/run.js`) passes — ALL tests green — run from a
  clean env (clear inherited `CREWS_*` + agent-session vars per crews AGENTS.md). This is the
  functional acceptance gate. (Perf note, NON-blocking: the suite historically completes in ~40-90s
  on Windows at default concurrency; a run materially over that is a flake/regression signal to
  investigate, not an acceptance failure.)

## Open Questions
- **Version number**: this adds a lead-side resolution capability (reply-to now resolves consumed
  inbox ids), so a MINOR bump (3.12.0 → 3.13.0) is recommended over a patch. Impl/lead may choose
  3.12.1 if treating it strictly as a bug fix. [INFERRED — recommend 3.13.0]
- **Seed phrasing reconciliation**: the task seed said "assert no ReplyToNotFoundError AND the
  resolution is recorded." Because proactive-reports are STRICT-ACK auto-exempt, "the resolution is
  recorded" for the proactive-report case means the resolver returns the inbox row and the outbox row
  persists `replyTo`/`hops` — NOT a `decision:"replied"` mailbox-decision row (none is written for an
  exempt entry). The decision-row form of "resolution recorded" is covered separately on a NON-exempt
  consumed message (AC2b). [Resolved via Phase-4 Copilot review.]
- The lead's reply to a consumed proactive-report resolves the entry and writes the outbox row, but
  does NOT currently route a notification back to the member (lead per-row routing is member-only).
  This plan preserves that behavior; routing the lead's reply back to the member is a deliberate
  out-of-scope follow-up.
